public_body: Dedham Public Library Board Of Trustees
overall: The AG found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the Marketing Committee was not a public body, the Board needed no open-session vote to end negotiations, and withholding of minutes was proper. No orders issued.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleges the Board created a subcommittee (the Marketing Committee) that posts no notice and keeps no minutes, as required by the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Based on the foregoing, we find that the Marketing Committee was not a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleges a quorum of Board members deliberated outside a noticed meeting at the December 4, 2015 Marketing Committee meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the topics discussed during the December 4, 2015 meeting did not concern the operation of the library, the Board did not engage in improper deliberation

allegations.summary: Complaint alleges the Board had to vote in open session before ending contract negotiations with the former Library Director in executive session.
Complaint alleges the Board withheld executive session minutes on the former Library Director's contract after the purpose for secrecy had expired.
allegations.key_passage: We disagree. Even though the decision to cease negotiations had been made, the Board could have reinitiated negotiations with Dr. Tricarico's up until the end of her employment, which ended on February 13.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleges the Board acted outside its authority; the Attorney General reviews only Open Meeting Law compliance.
allegations.key_passage: Because this allegation, even if proven true, would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review it.
